speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel loops with no rectal gas strongly point to Hirschsprung disease. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to visualize the transition zone between the aganglionic and ganglionic bowel segments. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal contrast enema rules out Hirschsprung disease, so I need to evaluate for other causes of distal obstruction. I will request a surgical consultation to consider conditions like meconium ileus or intestinal atresia. REQUEST TEST: Surgical_Consultation

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal contrast enema and surgical consult findings make mechanical obstruction like Hirschsprung's or atresia less likely, suggesting a metabolic cause such as cystic fibrosis. I will request sweat chloride testing to evaluate for cystic fibrosis. REQUEST TEST: Sweat_Chloride_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal sweat chloride results ruling out cystic fibrosis, I need to investigate other congenital causes of obstruction. I will request a barium swallow study to check for esophageal atresia or tracheoesophageal fistula. REQUEST TEST: Barium_Swallow

speaker: Doctor
text: With structural and metabolic causes ruled out, I suspect a functional motility disorder or neurological issue affecting the bowel. I need to assess the infant's neurological status and reflexes to determine if this is a central nervous system problem. REQUEST EXAM: Neurological_Exam

text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

text: The normal ultrasound rules out conditions like annular pancreas, leaving meconium ileus as a strong possibility despite the normal sweat test.
